source.text: Ἦσαν δὲ Ἕλληνές τινες ἐκ τῶν ἀναβαινόντων ἵνα προσκυνήσωσιν ἐν τῇ ἑορτῇ·

records.literal_gloss: There were now Greeks certain among the [ones] going up that they might worship at the feast;

en.L: Now there were certain Greeks among those going up so that they might worship at the feast;
en.B: Among those who went up to worship at the festival were some Greeks.
en.R: Some Greeks were among the people who had come up to Jerusalem to worship at the Passover festival.

es.L: Había ciertos griegos entre los que subían a adorar en la fiesta;
es.B: Entre los que subieron a adorar en la fiesta había algunos griegos.
es.R: Entre la gente que había subido a Jerusalén para adorar a Dios en la fiesta de la Pascua había algunos griegos.

sw.L: Basi palikuwa na Wagiriki kadhaa miongoni mwa wale waliokuwa wakipanda ili waabudu kwenye sikukuu;
sw.B: Miongoni mwa wale waliopanda kwenda kuabudu kwenye sikukuu walikuwemo baadhi ya Wagiriki.
sw.R: Baadhi ya Wagiriki walikuwa miongoni mwa watu waliokuja Yerusalemu kuabudu kwenye sikukuu ya Pasaka.

decisions.choice: Greeks: non-Jews, people of the Greek-speaking world
decisions.reason: The word is used of Gentiles in general, as in 7:35, where the speakers set "the Greeks" beside the Jews scattered among them. Greek-speaking Jews were called by a different word (Acts 6:1). These visitors are Gentiles, which is why their coming matters: Jesus answers it by speaking of his hour and of drawing all people to himself (12:23, 32).

decisions.choice: Gentiles who worshiped Israel's God and came up to Jerusalem for the feast
decisions.reason: Those "going up" are the pilgrims who went up to Jerusalem for the festival, the Passover of 11:55 and 12:1. Gentiles who honored the God of Israel without becoming Jews (Acts 10:2; 17:4) could worship in the outer court of the temple but not go further in. Whether these Greeks were such worshipers or full converts the text does not say; that they came to worship shows that they honored Israel's God.

decisions.choice: the Greeks come as the hour arrives: a first sign of the wider gathering
decisions.reason: The Pharisees have just said that "the world has gone after him" (12:19), and now people from beyond Israel come seeking him. Jesus had spoken of other sheep not of this fold (10:16), and John of gathering the scattered children of God (11:52). The scorn of 7:35, that he might go and teach the Greeks, turns out to point the way.

decisions.choice: festival (B, R); to Jerusalem, Passover (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced says "festival" for the feast. Readable names the place they went up to and the feast, which John has named in 11:55 and 12:1 (meaning decision m2). Balanced puts the Greeks at the end of the sentence, where the Greek puts the weight on them by naming them first.

decisions.choice: a Jerusalén, a Dios, de la Pascua
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable says where they went up and whom they worshiped.

source.text: οὗτοι οὖν προσῆλθον Φιλίππῳ τῷ ἀπὸ Βηθσαϊδὰ τῆς Γαλιλαίας, καὶ ἠρώτων αὐτὸν λέγοντες· Κύριε, θέλομεν τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἰδεῖν.

records.literal_gloss: These therefore came to Philip the [one] from Bethsaida of the Galilee, and were asking him saying, "Sir, we want the Jesus to see."

en.L: So these came to Philip, the [one] from Bethsaida of Galilee, and were asking him, saying, "Sir, we want to see Jesus."
en.B: These men came to Philip, whose home was Bethsaida in Galilee, and made a request of him: "Sir, we would like to see Jesus."
en.R: They went to Philip, who came from the town of Bethsaida in Galilee. They asked him, "Sir, we would like to meet Jesus."

es.L: Estos, pues, se acercaron a Felipe, el de Betsaida de Galilea, y le rogaban, diciendo: «Señor, queremos ver a Jesús».
es.B: Estos se acercaron a Felipe, que era de Betsaida de Galilea, y le pidieron: «Señor, quisiéramos ver a Jesús».
es.R: Fueron a ver a Felipe, que era del pueblo de Betsaida, en Galilea. Le pidieron: «Señor, nos gustaría conocer a Jesús».

sw.L: Basi hao walimwendea Filipo, yule wa Bethsaida ya Galilaya, wakamwomba, wakisema, "Tunataka, bwana, kumwona Yesu."
sw.B: Watu hao walimwendea Filipo, aliyekuwa mwenyeji wa Bethsaida ya Galilaya, wakamwomba: "Tungependa, bwana, kumwona Yesu."
sw.R: Walikwenda kwa Filipo, aliyetoka katika mji wa Bethsaida huko Galilaya. Wakamwomba, "Tungependa, bwana, kukutana na Yesu."

decisions.choice: Philip from Bethsaida: a disciple with a Greek name from a town on the edge of Gentile country
decisions.reason: Philip came from Bethsaida, the hometown of Andrew and Peter (1:44). The town lay at the north end of the Sea of Galilee, near the Jordan, close to lands where many Gentiles lived, and Philip, like Andrew, bears a Greek name. John does not say why the Greeks went to Philip; that he was approachable to Greek speakers is a likely reason, but it is a guess.

decisions.choice: Sir: a polite address to Philip
decisions.reason: The word is the ordinary courteous way to address a man, as in 4:11 and 20:15. Here it is spoken to Philip, not to Jesus, so nothing more than politeness is meant.

decisions.choice: we want to see Jesus: a request to meet him and speak with him
decisions.reason: The imperfect "were asking" suggests a request pressed politely. "See" here means to meet someone in person, not just to catch sight of him. John uses the same verb of the deeper seeing that comes with believing (1:39; 12:45; 14:9); the request may hint at that, but in the story it is a plain request for a meeting.

decisions.choice: meet (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "meet" because the Greeks want to talk with Jesus, not only to look at him (meaning decision m3). Literal and Balanced keep "see", the word John wrote.

decisions.choice: Señor (polite address)
decisions.reason: Here only a polite address to Philip (meaning decision m2); Spanish uses "Señor" for both, as elsewhere in John.

decisions.choice: conocer
decisions.reason: As in English: to meet him and speak with him (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: bwana, placed inside the sentence
decisions.reason: A polite "sir" to Philip, so "bwana" is placed inside the sentence and stays lowercase, as in John 4-6.

source.text: ἔρχεται ὁ Φίλιππος καὶ λέγει τῷ Ἀνδρέᾳ· ἔρχεται Ἀνδρέας καὶ Φίλιππος καὶ λέγουσιν τῷ Ἰησοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Comes the Philip and tells the Andrew; comes Andrew and Philip and they tell the Jesus.

en.L: Philip comes and tells Andrew; Andrew and Philip come and tell Jesus.
en.B: Philip went and told Andrew, and then Andrew and Philip went and told Jesus.
en.R: Philip went and told Andrew. Then the two of them went together and told Jesus.

es.L: Viene Felipe y se lo dice a Andrés; viene Andrés, y Felipe, y se lo dicen a Jesús.
es.B: Felipe fue y se lo dijo a Andrés, y luego Andrés y Felipe fueron y se lo dijeron a Jesús.
es.R: Felipe fue y se lo dijo a Andrés. Luego los dos fueron juntos a decírselo a Jesús.

sw.L: Filipo anakuja na kumwambia Andrea; Andrea na Filipo wanakuja na kumwambia Yesu.
sw.B: Filipo alikwenda akamwambia Andrea, kisha Andrea na Filipo wakaenda wakamwambia Yesu.
sw.R: Filipo alikwenda akamwambia Andrea. Kisha wote wawili wakaenda pamoja wakamwambia Yesu.

decisions.choice: Philip and Andrew: two disciples from the same town who bring people to Jesus
decisions.reason: Andrew and Philip appear together in 1:40-44 and 6:5-9, and both bring others to Jesus (1:41-42, 45; 6:8-9). Why Philip first goes to Andrew is not said. He may simply have wanted his fellow townsman with him, or he may have been unsure whether Gentiles should be brought to a Jewish teacher; the text gives no reason.

decisions.choice: the second "comes" is singular though two men are named: a common pattern, with no stress on Andrew
decisions.reason: When a verb stands before two subjects joined by "and", Greek often makes it agree with the first one named. Both men go to Jesus, as the plural "they tell" shows.

decisions.choice: went ... told (B, R); also answered (verse 23)
decisions.reason: John often tells a story in the present tense ("he comes", "he tells") for vividness. Literal keeps the present; Balanced and Readable use the past, as stories are normally told in this language. This applies to every such verb in the passage (verses 22 and 23).

decisions.choice: historic present at Literal; pretérito at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: As elsewhere in John: Literal keeps John's present ("dice", "ven"); Balanced and Readable use the pretérito. This applies throughout the passage.

source.text: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἀποκρίνεται αὐτοῖς λέγων· Ἐλήλυθεν ἡ ὥρα ἵνα δοξασθῇ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου.

records.literal_gloss: The but Jesus answers them saying, "Has come the hour that may be glorified the Son of the Man.

en.L: And Jesus answers them, saying, "The hour has come that the Son of Man may be glorified.
en.B: Jesus answered them, "The hour has come when the Son of Man is to be glorified.
en.R: Jesus answered, "The hour has come. Now the Son of Man will be glorified.

es.L: Y Jesús les responde, diciendo: «Ha llegado la hora de que el Hijo del Hombre sea glorificado.
es.B: Jesús les respondió: «Ha llegado la hora en que el Hijo del Hombre va a ser glorificado.
es.R: Jesús respondió: «Ha llegado la hora. Ahora el Hijo del Hombre será glorificado.

sw.L: Na Yesu anawajibu, akisema, "Saa imefika ili Mwana wa Adamu atukuzwe.
sw.B: Yesu akawajibu, "Saa imefika ambapo Mwana wa Adamu atatukuzwa.
sw.R: Yesu akajibu, "Saa imefika. Sasa Mwana wa Adamu atatukuzwa.

decisions.choice: the hour: the appointed time of Jesus's death and glorification, now arrived
decisions.reason: Until now John has said that Jesus's hour had not yet come (2:4; 7:30; 8:20). Here, for the first time, Jesus says that it has. From this point the hour is the time of his passing from this world to the Father (13:1; 17:1). This is the turning point of the Gospel.

decisions.choice: glorified: honored and shown for who he is, through his death, resurrection and return to the Father
decisions.reason: In John, Jesus is glorified when he is lifted up on the cross and raised and returns to the Father (7:39; 12:16; 13:31-32; 17:1, 5). The next verses make plain that the way to glory is death (12:24, 32-33). Glorify is a key term.

decisions.choice: answered them: Andrew and Philip, and perhaps the Greeks with them
decisions.reason: Jesus does not reply to the request directly, and John does not say whether the Greeks met him. His answer speaks to what their coming means: the hour has come, and through his death he will draw all people to himself (12:32). Those addressed are at least Andrew and Philip; soon the crowd is listening too (12:29).

decisions.choice: the Son of Man: the title Jesus uses of himself, from Daniel 7:13-14
decisions.reason: In Daniel 7 one like a son of man receives glory and a kingdom that will not pass away. In John the title is tied to being lifted up and glorified (3:14; 8:28; 13:31), and the crowd will ask about it (12:34).

decisions.choice: hour, at every level
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice keeps "hour" for Jesus's appointed time at Literal and Balanced. Readable may say "time", but in this passage the word comes three times (12:23, 27) and the link with "his hour had not yet come" is the point, so Readable keeps it too. Readable splits the sentence to make the purpose plain.

decisions.choice: hora, at every level
decisions.reason: The book-wide word for the appointed hour, now arrived (meaning decision m1).

source.text: ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἐὰν μὴ ὁ κόκκος τοῦ σίτου πεσὼν εἰς τὴν γῆν ἀποθάνῃ, αὐτὸς μόνος μένει· ἐὰν δὲ ἀποθάνῃ, πολὺν καρπὸν φέρει.

records.literal_gloss: Truly truly I say to you, if not the grain of the wheat having fallen into the earth should die, it alone remains; if but it should die, much fruit it bears.

en.L: Truly, truly I say to you, unless the grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, it remains alone; but if it dies, it bears much fruit.
en.B: Truly, truly, I tell you, if a grain of wheat does not fall into the ground and die, it stays just a single grain; but if it dies, it bears much fruit.
en.R: I tell you the truth: a grain of wheat must fall into the ground and die. If it does not, it stays just one seed by itself. But if it dies, it grows and produces a great harvest.

es.L: En verdad, en verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que, si el grano de trigo no cae en la tierra y muere, queda solo; pero si muere, lleva mucho fruto.
es.B: En verdad, en verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que, si un grano de trigo no cae en la tierra y muere, se queda en un solo grano; pero si muere, da mucho fruto.
es.R: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo la verdad: un grano de trigo tiene que caer en la tierra y morir. Si no muere, se queda siendo una sola semilla. Pero si muere, crece y produce una gran cosecha.

sw.L: Kweli kweli nawaambia, punje ya ngano isipoanguka ardhini na kufa, inakaa peke yake; lakini ikifa, inazaa matunda mengi.
sw.B: Kweli kweli nawaambia, punje ya ngano isipoanguka ardhini na kufa, inabaki punje moja tu; lakini ikifa, inazaa matunda mengi.
sw.R: Nawaambia ukweli: punje ya ngano lazima ianguke ardhini na kufa. Isipokufa, inabaki mbegu moja tu peke yake. Lakini ikifa, inaota na kuzaa mavuno makubwa.

decisions.choice: a seed picture: grain sown in the ground seems to die before it grows
decisions.reason: A grain of wheat kept in the storehouse stays as it is. Only when it is buried in the soil and is gone as a seed does it sprout and bear an ear with many grains. Paul uses the same picture for the resurrection (1 Corinthians 15:36-37).

decisions.choice: much fruit: the many who will have life through Jesus's death
decisions.reason: The picture applies first to Jesus: by dying he will bring life to many, including the Greeks who have just come (12:20, 32; 11:51-52). Verses 25-26 then apply it to those who follow him. "Bear fruit" returns in 15:2-8.

decisions.choice: remains alone: in its ordinary sense, stays a single grain
decisions.reason: The verb is John's word "remain", here in its everyday sense. The crowd will use it in 12:34: the Christ "remains forever". Jesus's picture answers them in advance: the grain that will not die remains alone.

decisions.choice: Truly, truly I say to you (L); Truly, truly, I tell you (B); I tell you the truth (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide rendering for John (see 1:51), recorded once in this passage.

decisions.choice: stays (B, R); a single grain, one seed by itself; a great harvest (R)
decisions.reason: Following the book-wide choice, the verb is "remain" in its theological sense and the natural word in ordinary senses; Literal keeps "remains" so that the echo in 12:34 shows (meaning decision m3). Readable puts the condition as a plain statement and says what fruit means for a grain of wheat. Balanced keeps "bears much fruit", the phrase of 15:5 and 15:8.

decisions.choice: En verdad, en verdad les digo (L, B); Les digo la verdad (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide rendering.

decisions.choice: queda (L); se queda (B, R)
decisions.reason: The ordinary sense of remaining (meaning decision m3), so not "permanecer".

source.text: ὁ φιλῶν τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ ἀπολλύει αὐτήν, καὶ ὁ μισῶν τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ τούτῳ εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον φυλάξει αὐτήν.

records.literal_gloss: The [one] loving the life of him loses it, and the [one] hating the life of him in the world this into life eternal will keep it.

en.L: The one who loves {{gender:their|his}} life loses it, and the one who hates {{gender:their|his}} life in this world will keep it into eternal life.
en.B: Whoever loves {{gender:their|his}} life is losing it, and whoever hates {{gender:their|his}} life in this world will keep it safe for eternal life.
en.R: People who love their own life more than anything will lose it. But people who hate their life in this world, and put it last, will keep it safe and have eternal life.

es.L: El que ama su vida, la pierde; y el que aborrece su vida en este mundo, la guardará para vida eterna.
es.B: El que ama su vida la está perdiendo, y el que odia su vida en este mundo la conservará para la vida eterna.
es.R: Los que aman su propia vida más que nada la perderán. Pero los que odian su vida en este mundo, y la ponen en último lugar, la conservarán a salvo y tendrán vida eterna.

sw.L: Anayeyapenda maisha yake huyapoteza, na anayeyachukia maisha yake katika ulimwengu huu atayalinda hadi uzima wa milele.
sw.B: Anayeyapenda maisha yake anayapoteza, na anayeyachukia maisha yake katika ulimwengu huu atayahifadhi salama hadi uzima wa milele.
sw.R: Watu wanaopenda maisha yao kuliko kitu kingine chochote watayapoteza. Lakini watu wanaochukia maisha yao katika ulimwengu huu, na kuyaweka mwisho, watayahifadhi salama na kupata uzima wa milele.

decisions.choice: love and hate: a way of saying which comes first, not of feeling
decisions.reason: In the Bible "hate" set against "love" often means to love less, to put second (Genesis 29:30-31; Malachi 1:2-3). Luke 14:26 has "hate father and mother" where Matthew 10:37 has "love more than me". Jesus does not ask for disgust at one's own life, but for a life that holds it loosely and puts him first, even to death.

decisions.choice: life: one's own self, the life a person lives
decisions.reason: The word means a person's life, the self who lives it. The same word comes again in 12:27 ("my soul is troubled"), where it is Jesus's inner self.

decisions.choice: the paradox of losing and keeping: clinging to life loses it, giving it up keeps it
decisions.reason: The other Gospels give the saying in similar words (Mark 8:35; Matthew 10:39; Luke 9:24; 17:33). "In this world" marks the life that is let go: life as this world measures it (key term, humanity organized against God). What is kept is kept for eternal life, the life of the age to come. The present "loses" says that such a person is already losing it.

decisions.choice: {{gender:their|his}}
decisions.reason: "The one who" and "whoever" mean any person, man or woman, so the pronoun takes the gender setting. Readable says "people ... their", which needs no setting.

decisions.choice: is losing (B); more than anything, and put it last (R); keep it safe (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced shows the present tense of "loses" (meaning decision m3). Readable keeps "love" and "hate" but explains the idiom (meaning decision m1). "Keep it safe" gives the sense of guarding that the verb has.

decisions.choice: no gender setting
decisions.reason: Spanish "su" has no gender, so "el que ama su vida" needs no setting.

decisions.choice: aborrece (L); odia (B, R)
decisions.reason: Every level keeps the strong word, as a way of saying which comes first (meaning decision m1); Readable adds "la ponen en último lugar", as in English.

decisions.choice: maisha yake, with no gender span; maisha for psychē
decisions.reason: The English needs "their" with "his" as the traditional alternative; Swahili "yake" (his or her) says nothing about sex, so there is no span here or anywhere in this chapter. As in 10:11, "maisha" (one's life) is used for this word, and "uzima" for eternal life.

source.text: ἐὰν ἐμοί τις διακονῇ ἐμοὶ ἀκολουθείτω, καὶ ὅπου εἰμὶ ἐγὼ ἐκεῖ καὶ ὁ διάκονος ὁ ἐμὸς ἔσται· ἐάν τις ἐμοὶ διακονῇ τιμήσει αὐτὸν ὁ πατήρ.

records.literal_gloss: If me anyone serves, me let him follow, and where am I, there also the servant the my will be; if anyone me serves, will honor him the Father.

en.L: If anyone serves {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, let {{gender:them|him}} follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; and where I am, there also {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant will be. If anyone serves {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, the Father will honor {{gender:them|him}}.
en.B: Anyone who serves {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} must follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant will be where I am. The Father will honor anyone who serves {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: Anyone who serves {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} must follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. My servant will be with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} wherever I am. And the Father will honor anyone who serves {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

es.L: Si alguno me sirve, que me siga; y donde yo estoy, allí también estará mi servidor. Si alguno me sirve, el Padre lo honrará.
es.B: El que me sirva, que me siga; y donde yo esté, allí estará también mi servidor. Al que me sirva, el Padre lo honrará.
es.R: El que quiera servirme tiene que seguirme. Mi servidor estará conmigo dondequiera que yo esté. Y el Padre honrará al que me sirva.

sw.L: Mtu yeyote akinitumikia, na anifuate; na mahali nilipo {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, ndipo atakapokuwa mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}. Mtu yeyote akinitumikia, Baba atamheshimu.
sw.B: Yeyote anayenitumikia lazima anifuate, na mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} atakuwa pale nilipo. Baba atamheshimu yeyote anayenitumikia.
sw.R: Yeyote anayenitumikia lazima anifuate. Mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} atakuwa pamoja nami popote nilipo. Na Baba atamheshimu yeyote anayenitumikia.

decisions.choice: serve, servant: one who works for another and attends to his needs
decisions.reason: The verb and the noun are the words for serving, used of waiting at table (2:5, 9; 12:2) and of service in general. They are not the word for a slave, a person owned by another (8:34-35). The stress is on attending to Jesus, which here means going where he goes.

decisions.choice: follow me ... where I am: go the way Jesus goes, through death to the Father, and share his place
decisions.reason: Following Jesus, coming right after the saying about the grain and about losing one's life, means going his way, even to death (13:36-37; 21:18-19). "Where I am" points to where he is going, the Father's presence; he promises that his own will be with him there (14:3; 17:24).

decisions.choice: let him follow: a command, what serving Jesus requires
decisions.reason: The third-person command does not grant permission; it sets the condition. Whoever serves Jesus must follow him.

decisions.choice: the Father will honor him: honor given by God, not by people
decisions.reason: Jesus has said that people seek honor from one another rather than from God (5:41-44). Those who serve him receive honor from the Father himself, as the Son does (8:54).

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}
decisions.reason: Every pronoun for Christ or for God uses the deity_pronoun setting, including "me" and "my" when Jesus speaks of himself, "your" when he speaks to the Father, and "you" when people speak to him. At the start of a sentence "He" is written plain. This applies throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: servant; let them follow (L); Anyone who serves me must follow me (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Servant" is the plain word for this noun at every level; the other word, for one who is owned, is "slave" in Literal (meaning decision m1). Literal gives the pronoun the gender setting, since "anyone" means a man or a woman; Balanced and Readable state the command with "anyone who ... must", which needs no pronoun.

decisions.choice: servidor
decisions.reason: One who serves another (meaning decision m1); "esclavo" is kept for the other Greek word (8:34-35). "Lo" is a clitic and takes no gender setting.

source.text: Νῦν ἡ ψυχή μου τετάρακται, καὶ τί εἴπω;

records.literal_gloss: Now the soul of me has been troubled, and what may I say?

en.L: Now {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} soul has been troubled, and what shall I say?
en.B: Now {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} soul is troubled, and what should I say?
en.R: Now {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} heart is troubled. What should I say?

es.L: Ahora mi alma está turbada, ¿y qué diré?
es.B: Ahora mi alma está turbada, ¿y qué voy a decir?
es.R: Ahora mi corazón está angustiado. ¿Qué debo decir?

sw.L: Sasa roho {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} imefadhaika, nami niseme nini?
sw.B: Sasa roho {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} imefadhaika, nami niseme nini?
sw.R: Sasa moyo {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} umefadhaika. Niseme nini?

decisions.choice: my soul is troubled: Jesus is shaken and distressed in his inner self
decisions.reason: The word for soul is the one translated "life" in 12:25: the self, here as the seat of feeling. The verb for troubled is used of Jesus at Lazarus's tomb (11:33) and at the foretelling of Judas's betrayal (13:21). The perfect tense says he has become troubled and remains so. John does not hide Jesus's anguish at the death ahead of him.

decisions.choice: an echo of the Psalms of distress
decisions.reason: In the Greek of Psalm 6:4-5 the psalmist says that his soul is greatly troubled and asks God to save him; Psalm 42:6-7 and 12 also speak of a downcast, troubled soul. Jesus's words come close to these prayers in both wording and order (troubled soul, then save me). John does not mark a quotation, so the echo is likely but not certain.

decisions.choice: what shall I say: a real deliberative question, Jesus weighing what to pray
decisions.reason: The subjunctive asks what he is to say. In the SBLGNT the question ends here, and the next words are his answer (see the note on the next sentence).

decisions.choice: heart (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "heart", the everyday word for the inner self where feelings are felt (meaning decision m1). Literal and Balanced keep "soul".

decisions.choice: corazón
decisions.reason: As in English: the inner self (meaning decision m1).

source.text: πάτερ, σῶσόν με ἐκ τῆς ὥρας ταύτης.

records.literal_gloss: Father, save me out of the hour this.

en.L: Father, save {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} from this hour.
en.B: Father, save {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} from this hour.
en.R: Father, save {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} from this hour!

es.L: Padre, sálvame de esta hora.
es.B: Padre, sálvame de esta hora.
es.R: ¡Padre, sálvame de esta hora!

sw.L: Baba, niokoe na saa hii.
sw.B: Baba, niokoe na saa hii.
sw.R: Baba, niokoe na saa hii!

decisions.choice: a real prayer, as the SBLGNT punctuates it: Jesus prays to be saved from the hour, then sets the prayer aside
alternatives: a prayer considered and rejected: "Shall I say, 'Father, save me from this hour'?"
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT ends the question at "what shall I say?" and prints "Father, save me from this hour" as a sentence of its own, ending in a full stop. Read so, Jesus truly asks to be spared and at once turns: "But for this reason I came to this hour." The other reading makes it part of the question: "Shall I say, 'Father, save me from this hour'?", a prayer he considers and refuses. The ancient manuscripts had no punctuation, so both readings are possible, and the sense of the passage is the same: Jesus faces the hour and chooses the Father's glory.

decisions.choice: save me from this hour: spare me from the death that is coming
alternatives: bring me safely through this hour
decisions.reason: "This hour" is the hour of 12:23, his death. "Save me out of" most naturally asks to be kept from it, which is why the next words turn against it. Hebrews 5:7 speaks of Jesus praying to the one able to save him out of death, which is sometimes taken to mean bringing him safely through death rather than sparing him from it.

decisions.choice: John's counterpart to the prayer in Gethsemane
decisions.reason: Mark tells how Jesus, his soul very sorrowful, prayed that "the hour might pass from him" and said "Father, ... remove this cup from me; yet not what I will, but what you will" (Mark 14:34-36). John does not tell that scene, but here are the same troubled soul, the same hour, the same prayer to the Father, and the same yielding. Whether John means his readers to recall it is not certain.

decisions.choice: a prayer in its own sentence, with no quotation marks inside Jesus's words
decisions.reason: Following the SBLGNT punctuation (meaning decision m1), every level gives the prayer as words Jesus actually prays, not as a quoted option. Readable ends it with an exclamation mark to show the cry before the turn that follows. The footnote gives the reading as a question.

decisions.choice: a prayer in its own sentence, with no inner quotation marks
decisions.reason: As in English: a real prayer (meaning decision m1).

source.text: ἀλλὰ διὰ τοῦτο ἦλθον εἰς τὴν ὥραν ταύτην.

records.literal_gloss: But on account of this I came into the hour this.

en.L: But on account of this I came to this hour.
en.B: But it was for this very reason that I came to this hour.
en.R: But no. This is the very reason I came: to face this hour.

es.L: Pero por esto vine a esta hora.
es.B: Pero precisamente para esto he llegado a esta hora.
es.R: Pero no. Precisamente para esto vine: para enfrentar esta hora.

sw.L: Lakini kwa sababu hii nilikuja hadi saa hii.
sw.B: Lakini ni kwa sababu hii hasa nilikuja hadi saa hii.
sw.R: Lakini hapana. Hii ndiyo sababu hasa niliyokuja: ili niikabili saa hii.

decisions.choice: for this reason: to go through this hour, for the purpose he names next
decisions.reason: "This" points both back and forward. Jesus came to this hour for the very purpose of the hour itself, his death, and for what it serves: the glory of the Father's name (12:28).

decisions.choice: the cross is the purpose of Jesus's coming, not something that happens to him
decisions.reason: Jesus lays down his life of his own accord (10:17-18) and will not refuse the cup the Father has given him (18:11). He came into the world for this (18:37). The "but" turns from the cry of 12:27 to obedience.

decisions.choice: it was for this very reason (B); But no ... to face this hour (R)
alternatives: But for this purpose I came to this hour
decisions.reason: Balanced puts emphasis on "for this", as the Greek order does. Readable adds "no" to make the turn from the prayer clear, and "to face" to say what coming to the hour means (meaning decisions m1-m2).

decisions.choice: precisamente para esto (B); Pero no ... para enfrentar esta hora (R)
decisions.reason: As in English.

source.text: πάτερ, δόξασόν σου τὸ ὄνομα.

records.literal_gloss: Father, glorify of you the name."

en.L: Father, glorify {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name."
en.B: Father, glorify {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name."
en.R: Father, bring glory to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name!"

es.L: Padre, glorifica tu nombre».
es.B: Padre, glorifica tu nombre».
es.R: ¡Padre, muestra la gloria de tu nombre!».

sw.L: Baba, litukuze jina {{deity_pronoun:lako|Lako}}."
sw.B: Baba, litukuze jina {{deity_pronoun:lako|Lako}}."
sw.R: Baba, lipe jina {{deity_pronoun:lako|Lako}} utukufu!"

decisions.choice: glorify your name: show who the Father is, in his greatness and love, through what is about to happen
decisions.reason: A name in the Bible stands for the person as he has made himself known (17:6, 26; Psalm 115:1). Jesus's second prayer replaces the first: not escape, but the Father's glory, which will be shown in the Son's death and exaltation (13:31-32; 17:1, 4).

decisions.choice: a prayer like the opening of the Lord's Prayer
decisions.reason: "Father, glorify your name" is close to "Father, may your name be honored" (Matthew 6:9; Luke 11:2). The likeness may be only that both pray for God's name; John does not quote the prayer.

decisions.choice: bring glory to (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "bring glory to", which keeps the key term and is clearer in everyday speech than "glorify".

decisions.choice: muestra la gloria de
decisions.reason: As in English: says what glorifying the name means (meaning decision m1).

source.text: ἦλθεν οὖν φωνὴ ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ· Καὶ ἐδόξασα καὶ πάλιν δοξάσω.

records.literal_gloss: Came therefore a voice out of the heaven, "Both I glorified [it] and again I will glorify [it]."

en.L: So a voice came out of heaven, "I both glorified [it] and will glorify [it] again."
en.B: Then a voice came out of heaven: "I have glorified it and will glorify it again."
en.R: Then a voice spoke from heaven: "I have brought glory to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, and I will bring glory to it again."

es.L: Vino, pues, una voz del cielo: «Lo glorifiqué, y lo glorificaré otra vez».
es.B: Entonces vino una voz del cielo: «Ya lo he glorificado, y lo glorificaré otra vez».
es.R: Entonces se oyó una voz del cielo que decía: «Ya he mostrado la gloria de mi nombre, y la volveré a mostrar».

sw.L: Basi sauti ikatoka mbinguni, "Nimelitukuza [jina], na nitalitukuza tena."
sw.B: Kisha sauti ikatoka mbinguni: "Nimelitukuza, nami nitalitukuza tena."
sw.R: Kisha sauti ikasema kutoka mbinguni: "Nimelipa jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} utukufu, nami nitalipa utukufu tena."

decisions.choice: a voice from heaven: God the Father speaking
decisions.reason: Heaven stands for God himself. A voice from heaven speaks at Jesus's baptism and transfiguration in the other Gospels (Mark 1:11; 9:7). Here it answers Jesus's prayer at once.

decisions.choice: I have glorified it and will glorify it again: in Jesus's life and signs, and in his death and exaltation
decisions.reason: The Father's name has already been glorified in what Jesus has done, his signs revealing God's glory (2:11; 11:4, 40; 17:4). It will be glorified again in the hour now come, the cross, resurrection and return to the Father (13:31-32; 17:1, 5).

decisions.choice: the unstated object is the Father's name
decisions.reason: Neither verb has an object; both answer "glorify your name" in the line before.

decisions.choice: [it] (L); it (B); my name ... it (R)
decisions.reason: The object is supplied (meaning decision m3): in brackets at Literal, plainly at Balanced, and named at Readable, where the Father speaks of his own name.

decisions.choice: lo (L, B); mi nombre (R)
decisions.reason: Spanish needs the object pronoun, so Literal does not bracket it; Readable names the Father's name (meaning decision m3).

source.text: ὁ οὖν ὄχλος ὁ ἑστὼς καὶ ἀκούσας ἔλεγεν βροντὴν γεγονέναι· ἄλλοι ἔλεγον· Ἄγγελος αὐτῷ λελάληκεν.

records.literal_gloss: The therefore crowd the [one] having stood and having heard was saying thunder to have happened; others were saying, "An angel to him has spoken."

en.L: So the crowd that was standing [there] and had heard was saying that it had thundered; others were saying, "An angel has spoken to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."
en.B: The crowd that stood there and heard it said it had thundered. Others were saying, "An angel has spoken to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."
en.R: The crowd standing there heard the sound. Some of them said it was thunder. Others said, "An angel has spoken to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."

es.L: La multitud, pues, que estaba [allí] y [lo] había oído, decía que había sido un trueno; otros decían: «Un ángel le ha hablado».
es.B: La multitud que estaba allí y lo oyó decía que había tronado. Otros decían: «Un ángel le ha hablado».
es.R: La gente que estaba allí oyó el sonido. Algunos decían que había sido un trueno. Otros decían: «Un ángel le ha hablado».

sw.L: Basi umati uliokuwa umesimama [pale] na kusikia ulikuwa ukisema kwamba ngurumo imetokea; wengine walikuwa wakisema, "Malaika amesema {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}."
sw.B: Umati uliosimama pale na kusikia ulisema kwamba imenguruma. Wengine walikuwa wakisema, "Malaika amesema {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}."
sw.R: Umati uliosimama pale ulisikia sauti hiyo. Baadhi yao walisema ni ngurumo. Wengine walisema, "Malaika amesema {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}."

decisions.choice: the crowd heard a sound but did not grasp what was said
decisions.reason: The crowd heard something, but some took it for thunder, and others knew it was speech without receiving it as God's own word. John does not say whether any of them made out the words. In the same way the companions of Paul heard a sound but did not understand the voice (Acts 9:7; 22:9).

decisions.choice: thunder and angels: ways people of the time thought God might speak
decisions.reason: In Scripture thunder goes with God's voice (Exodus 19:16-19; 2 Samuel 22:14; Psalm 29:3; Job 37:4-5), and angels bring God's word to people (Genesis 22:11; Luke 1:13). Both groups sense that something from heaven has happened, yet neither hears the Father answering his Son.

decisions.choice: the sound; Some of them
decisions.reason: Readable says the crowd heard a sound, and adds "some of them" to set beside "others": the Greek says the crowd said one thing and others another (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: el sonido; Algunos
decisions.reason: As in English (meaning decision m1).

source.text: ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς καὶ εἶπεν· Οὐ δι’ ἐμὲ ἡ φωνὴ αὕτη γέγονεν ἀλλὰ δι’ ὑμᾶς.

records.literal_gloss: Answered Jesus and said, "Not because of me the voice this has come but because of you.

en.L: Jesus answered and said, "Not because of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} has this voice come, but because of you.
en.B: Jesus answered, "This voice came for your sake, not for {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}}.
en.R: Jesus answered, "This voice did not speak for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sake. It spoke to help you.

es.L: Respondió Jesús y dijo: «No ha venido esta voz por causa de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, sino por causa de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.B: Jesús respondió: «Esta voz ha venido por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, no por {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.
es.R: Jesús respondió: «Esta voz no habló por {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}. Habló para {{plural_you:ayudarlos|ayudaros}}.

sw.L: Yesu akajibu, akasema, "Sauti hii haikuja kwa ajili {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, bali kwa ajili yenu.
sw.B: Yesu akajibu, "Sauti hii ilikuja kwa ajili yenu, si kwa ajili {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}.
sw.R: Yesu akajibu, "Sauti hii haikusema kwa ajili {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}. Ilisema ili kuwasaidia ninyi.

decisions.choice: for your sake: so that the crowd might believe that the Father sent Jesus
decisions.reason: Jesus did not need the voice to know that the Father hears him. At Lazarus's tomb he gave thanks aloud for the same reason, "because of the crowd standing around, so that they may believe that you sent me" (11:42).

decisions.choice: not ... but: a sharp contrast that puts the whole purpose on the hearers
decisions.reason: The voice was not given for Jesus's sake at all, but for theirs. Even so, most of them did not understand it (12:29), and few believed (12:37).

decisions.choice: This voice came for your sake, not for mine (B); did not speak for my sake. It spoke to help you (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the positive part first, the natural order for this kind of contrast; Literal keeps the Greek order. Readable says what "for your sake" means in two short sentences.

decisions.choice: por ustedes, no por mí (B); no habló por mí. Habló para ayudarlos (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: puts the stress on the hearers (meaning decision m2).

source.text: νῦν κρίσις ἐστὶν τοῦ κόσμου τούτου, νῦν ὁ ἄρχων τοῦ κόσμου τούτου ἐκβληθήσεται ἔξω·

records.literal_gloss: Now judgment is of the world this, now the ruler of the world this will be cast out;

en.L: Now is [the] judgment of this world; now the ruler of this world will be cast out.
en.B: Now is the time of judgment for this world; now the ruler of this world will be driven out.
en.R: Now is the time for this world to be judged. Now Satan, the ruler of this world, will be thrown out.

es.L: Ahora es [el] juicio de este mundo; ahora el gobernante de este mundo será echado fuera.
es.B: Ahora es el momento del juicio de este mundo; ahora el gobernante de este mundo será expulsado.
es.R: Ahora es el momento en que este mundo será juzgado. Ahora Satanás, el que gobierna este mundo, será echado fuera.

sw.L: Sasa ni hukumu ya ulimwengu huu; sasa mtawala wa ulimwengu huu atatupwa nje.
sw.B: Sasa ni wakati wa hukumu kwa ulimwengu huu; sasa mtawala wa ulimwengu huu atafukuzwa nje.
sw.R: Sasa ni wakati wa ulimwengu huu kuhukumiwa. Sasa Shetani, mtawala wa ulimwengu huu, atatupwa nje.

decisions.choice: now is the judgment: the world is judged at the cross, in the hour that has come
decisions.reason: "Now" is the hour of 12:23. By the way it treats Jesus, the world shows what it is and is judged (3:18-19), and the ruler of this world is condemned (16:11). The same events are the world's judgment and the defeat of its ruler.

decisions.choice: world: humanity organized against God
decisions.reason: Both times here "this world" is not the created order but human life as it stands apart from God and under a ruler opposed to him (15:18-19; 17:14). World is a key term.

decisions.choice: the ruler of this world: Satan
decisions.reason: Jesus calls him so again in 14:30 and 16:11. He is the devil, who puts it into Judas's heart to betray Jesus (13:2, 27). Paul uses a similar title (2 Corinthians 4:4; Ephesians 2:2). Being cast out means losing his hold over the world.

decisions.choice: will be cast out (SBLGNT)
alternatives: will be cast down (a few witnesses)
decisions.reason: A few witnesses, among them some early versions, read "will be cast down" instead of "cast out". Nearly all manuscripts read "out", and the sense is close. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the time of judgment (B); the time for this world to be judged; Satan (R); driven out (B); thrown out (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "the time" to show that "now" means this moment, the hour. Readable names Satan, whom the title means (meaning decision m3); the speaker is Jesus, who knows who the ruler is. "Driven out" and "thrown out" say what being cast out means today.

decisions.choice: el gobernante (L, B); Satanás, el que gobierna (R)
decisions.reason: "El príncipe de este mundo" is the traditional wording, but "príncipe" now suggests a king's son; "gobernante" is the word used for rulers at 3:1 and 7:26.

decisions.choice: el momento
decisions.reason: As in English; "hora" is kept for the Greek word for hour.

source.text: κἀγὼ ἐὰν ὑψωθῶ ἐκ τῆς γῆς, πάντας ἑλκύσω πρὸς ἐμαυτόν.

records.literal_gloss: And I if I am lifted up out of the earth, all I will draw to myself."

en.L: And I, if I am lifted up from the earth, will draw all [people] to {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}}."
en.B: As for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, when I am lifted up from the earth, I will draw all people to {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}}."
en.R: And when I am lifted up from the earth, I will draw all people to {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}}."

es.L: Y yo, si soy levantado en alto desde la tierra, atraeré a todos a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} mismo».
es.B: En cuanto a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, cuando sea levantado en alto desde la tierra, atraeré a todos hacia {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}».
es.R: Y cuando yo sea levantado en alto desde la tierra, atraeré a todos hacia {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}».

sw.L: Nami, ikiwa nitainuliwa kutoka duniani, nitawavuta [watu] wote {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}} {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}}."
sw.B: Na kwa upande {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, nitakapoinuliwa kutoka duniani, nitawavuta watu wote {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}} {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}}."
sw.R: Nami nitakapoinuliwa kutoka duniani, nitawavuta watu wote {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}} {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}}."

decisions.choice: lifted up: raised on the cross, and by that exalted
decisions.reason: As in 3:14 and 8:28, the verb means both to raise something high and to exalt someone. The next verse says that it points to the kind of death Jesus would die, and "from the earth" fits being raised on a cross; but in the Greek of Isaiah 52:13 the LORD's servant "will be lifted up and glorified", and here the lifting up draws all people to him. Every level keeps "lifted up" with both senses.

decisions.choice: if I am lifted up: a sure event, not a doubtful one
decisions.reason: "If" here means "when", as in 14:3 ("if I go and prepare a place for you"). Jesus has no doubt it will happen. "And I" is emphatic: set against the ruler of this world cast out (12:31), Jesus will be lifted up and draw people to himself.

decisions.choice: all: all people, Gentiles as well as Jews
decisions.reason: The word is masculine and refers to people. Coming just after the Greeks' request (12:20-23), it means that people of every nation, not only Israel, will be drawn to Jesus (10:16; 11:52). John does not say here that every person will believe; the next verses tell of many who did not (12:37).

decisions.choice: all people (SBLGNT)
decisions.reason: A few important manuscripts, among them P66 and the first hand of Codex Sinaiticus, with some early Latin copies, read the neuter "all things". The great majority read "all people", which fits the context of the Greeks' coming. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: draw: bring people to himself by his own power
decisions.reason: The same verb is used in 6:44, where no one can come to Jesus unless the Father draws him. Now Jesus, lifted up, does the drawing. The verb is also used of hauling in a net full of fish (21:6, 11).

decisions.choice: lifted up, with no "on the cross"; As for me, when (B); all [people] (L); all people (B, R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice keeps "lifted up" at every level with no addition, as at 3:14 and 8:28; the narrator explains it in the next verse (meaning decision m1). Balanced shows the emphatic "I" with "As for me" and says "when" (meaning decision m2). "All people" already includes men and women and needs no gender setting.

decisions.choice: levantado en alto, with no "en la cruz"; a todos
decisions.reason: The book-wide wording (3:14, 8:28), which keeps both senses, raised on the cross and exalted (meaning decision m1). Spanish "todos" already means all people, so Literal brackets nothing.

decisions.choice: nitainuliwa / nitakapoinuliwa, with no "msalabani"
decisions.reason: As at 3:14, "kuinuliwa" means both to be lifted up and to be raised to honour, so it keeps the double sense; verse 33 explains it. The same in verse 34.

source.text: τοῦτο δὲ ἔλεγεν σημαίνων ποίῳ θανάτῳ ἤμελλεν ἀποθνῄσκειν.

records.literal_gloss: This now he was saying signifying by what kind of death he was about to die.

en.L: Now this {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was saying, signifying by what kind of death {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was about to die.
en.B: He said this to show what kind of death {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was going to die.
en.R: He said this to show how {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was going to die: lifted up on a cross.

es.L: Y esto decía, dando a entender de qué muerte iba a morir.
es.B: Dijo esto para indicar qué clase de muerte iba a sufrir.
es.R: Dijo esto para mostrar cómo iba a morir: levantado en una cruz.

sw.L: Basi alisema hivi, akionyesha ni kifo cha namna gani atakachokufa.
sw.B: Alisema hivi kuonyesha ni kifo cha namna gani atakachokufa.
sw.R: Alisema hivi kuonyesha jinsi atakavyokufa: akiinuliwa juu ya msalaba.

decisions.choice: the narrator explains Jesus's words
decisions.reason: John steps out of the scene to tell the reader what "lifted up" means. He uses the same phrase again in 18:32, when Pilate's handing Jesus over leads to crucifixion, and of Peter's death in 21:19.

decisions.choice: what kind of death: crucifixion, death by being raised up on a cross
decisions.reason: The Jewish authorities could not lawfully put a man to death (18:31-32), and the Roman form of execution was crucifixion, in which the condemned was raised on a cross. "Lifted up from the earth" pointed to this. "Signifying" means indicating by a hint rather than saying outright.

decisions.choice: lifted up on a cross (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what kind of death was meant (meaning decision m2). The narrator, not Jesus, gives this explanation, so the addition puts no knowledge into a character's mouth.

decisions.choice: levantado en una cruz
decisions.reason: As in English (meaning decision m2).

source.text: ἀπεκρίθη οὖν αὐτῷ ὁ ὄχλος· Ἡμεῖς ἠκούσαμεν ἐκ τοῦ νόμου ὅτι ὁ χριστὸς μένει εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα, καὶ πῶς λέγεις σὺ ὅτι δεῖ ὑψωθῆναι τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου;

records.literal_gloss: Answered therefore him the crowd, "We heard out of the law that the Christ remains into the age, and how say you that it is necessary to be lifted up the Son of the Man?

en.L: So the crowd answered {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "We have heard from the Law that the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} remains forever, and how do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} say that it is necessary for the Son of Man to be lifted up?
en.B: The crowd answered {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "We have heard from the Law that the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} remains forever. So how can {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} tell us that the Son of Man must be lifted up?
en.R: The crowd answered {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "The Law tells us that the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} will remain forever. So why do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} say the Son of Man has to be lifted up?

es.L: Le respondió, pues, la multitud: «Nosotros hemos oído de la ley que el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}} permanece para siempre; ¿y cómo dices {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} que es necesario que el Hijo del Hombre sea levantado en alto?
es.B: La multitud le respondió: «Hemos oído en la ley que el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}} permanece para siempre. Entonces, ¿cómo puedes decir {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} que el Hijo del Hombre tiene que ser levantado en alto?

sw.L: Basi umati ukamjibu, "Sisi tumesikia kutoka katika Sheria kwamba {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} anakaa milele, nawe unasemaje kwamba imempasa Mwana wa Adamu kuinuliwa?

decisions.choice: the Law: the Scriptures as a whole
decisions.reason: "The Law" here is not only the books of Moses but the Scriptures generally, as in 10:34 and 15:25, where Psalms are quoted as the Law.

decisions.choice: the Christ remains forever: the promise of an everlasting king from David's line
decisions.reason: No single verse says these words. In the Greek of Psalm 89:37-38 David's offspring "will remain forever"; Isaiah 9:7 promises a kingdom with no end, Ezekiel 37:25 that David will be prince forever, and Daniel 7:14 that the dominion of the one like a son of man will not pass away. Which passage the crowd had in mind is uncertain.

decisions.choice: the crowd takes "lifted up" to mean being taken away by death
decisions.reason: They understand enough to see that Jesus speaks of leaving the earth, and that does not fit a Messiah who remains forever. They put together his words about the Son of Man (12:23) and about being lifted up (12:32). Their "remains" echoes Jesus's grain that "remains alone" unless it dies (12:24).

decisions.choice: the Christ: the title, God's anointed King
decisions.reason: With the article it is a title, the Messiah the people were waiting for (1:20, 41; 7:41-42).

decisions.choice: So how can you tell us (B); So why do you say ... has to (R); must (B); The Law tells us (R)
alternatives: How is it that you say (Literal)
decisions.reason: The question "how do you say" is a protest, not a request for information; Balanced and Readable put it as English protests, as at 8:33. "Must" (Balanced) and "has to" (Readable) for "it is necessary", as at 3:14. Readable says "tells us" for "we have heard from".

decisions.choice: la ley; permanece
decisions.reason: "La ley" here means the Scriptures as a whole (meaning decision m1), lowercase as at 7:19 and 10:34. "Permanecer" for the weighty sense of remaining.

decisions.choice: a puzzled question: what kind of Son of Man is this, who must be lifted up?
decisions.reason: The crowd is not asking for a definition of the title. They cannot fit a Son of Man who must die with the Messiah they expect, so they ask what figure Jesus can mean. Their question may also carry doubt about Jesus himself.

decisions.choice: Jesus does not answer directly
decisions.reason: He has already told the man born blind who the Son of Man is (9:35-37). Here he answers by urging them to believe in the light while they have it (12:35-36).

decisions.choice: 'Son of Man' in quotation marks (R)
decisions.reason: Readable marks the title as the words Jesus used that the crowd is now asking about (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: “Hijo del Hombre” in inner quotation marks (R)
decisions.reason: As in English.

decisions.choice: the light: Jesus himself, present among them
decisions.reason: Jesus has called himself the light of the world (8:12; 9:5; compare 1:4-9). "Among you" means present with them, not within them. Instead of answering "who is this Son of Man?" he tells them that the one they question is the light, and that he will not be with them long.

decisions.choice: a little while longer: the short time before his death
decisions.reason: Jesus has spoken this way before (7:33) and will again (13:33; 16:16). His hour has come (12:23); the time to respond is short.

decisions.choice: The light is among you (B) / with you (R) for only a little while longer
alternatives: Yet a little time the light is among you (Literal)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable start with "the light" and put the time at the end, the natural order; Literal keeps the Greek order. Readable says "with you", which is simpler and means the same here (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: La luz estará entre ustedes (B) / con ustedes (R) solo un poco más
decisions.reason: As in English.

en.R: Walk by the light while you have it, so that the darkness does not catch up with you. People who walk in the dark do not know where they are going.

sw.L: Tembeeni maadamu mnayo nuru, ili giza lisiwapate; na anayetembea gizani hajui anakokwenda.
sw.B: Tembeeni maadamu mnayo nuru, ili giza lisiwakute. Yeyote anayetembea gizani hajui anakokwenda.
sw.R: Tembeeni kwa nuru maadamu mnayo, ili giza lisiwafikie. Watu wanaotembea gizani hawajui wanakokwenda.

decisions.choice: walk: live, conduct one's life
decisions.reason: In the Bible "walk" often means how a person lives. Jesus continues the picture of 11:9-10: the one who walks by day does not stumble. To walk while they have the light is to follow Jesus and live by him while he is with them (8:12; 1 John 1:6-7).

decisions.choice: overtake: darkness coming upon them and seizing them
decisions.reason: The verb means to seize or catch up with. It is the same verb as in 1:5, where the darkness did not overcome the light; here the darkness may overcome those who do not walk in the light.

decisions.choice: the one who walks in darkness does not know where he is going
decisions.reason: Jesus knows where he came from and where he is going (8:14; 13:3). Whoever rejects the light has no such knowledge and is lost, like someone walking at night (11:10; 1 John 2:11).

decisions.choice: while (SBLGNT)
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts have a different word here and in 12:36 meaning "while" or "until". The SBLGNT reading, with the older witnesses, also means "while" in this context, so the sense is the same. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: {{gender:they are|he is}}
decisions.reason: "The one who walks" and "anyone who walks" mean any person, man or woman, so the pronoun takes the gender setting. Readable says "people ... they", which needs no setting.

decisions.choice: Walk by the light; catch up with (R)
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the picture of walking but adds "by the light" so the picture is clear (meaning decision m1), and uses the everyday "catch up with" for "overtake".

decisions.choice: no gender setting
decisions.reason: "No sabe adónde va" needs no pronoun in Spanish.

decisions.choice: la oscuridad; alcance (L, B); atrape (R)
decisions.reason: "La oscuridad" as in 1:5 and 8:12.

sw.B: Maadamu mnayo nuru, iaminini nuru, ili mpate kuwa wana wa nuru."
sw.R: Maadamu mnayo nuru, iaminini nuru. Ndipo mtakuwa watu walio wa nuru."

decisions.choice: sons of light: people who belong to the light and share its nature
decisions.reason: "Son of" something is a Hebrew way of saying that a person belongs to it or is marked by it. "Sons of light" are people who belong to God's light and live by it (Luke 16:8; 1 Thessalonians 5:5; Ephesians 5:8). The phrase includes women and men alike.

decisions.choice: believe in the light: believe in Jesus, and so become one of God's people
decisions.reason: The light is Jesus (12:35). Believing in him makes people children of God (1:12) and gives them the light of life (8:12). "Become" says that this is a new belonging, not something they have by birth.

decisions.choice: {{gender:children|sons}} of light
decisions.reason: The phrase means people of either sex (meaning decision m1), so it takes the gender setting, with the traditional "sons" as the alternative.

decisions.choice: people who belong to the light (R)
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom (meaning decision m1) instead of reproducing it; this wording already includes everyone and needs no setting.

decisions.choice: hijos de luz, no setting
decisions.reason: As at 1:12: Spanish "hijos" is the ordinary word for sons and daughters.

decisions.choice: gente que pertenece a la luz
decisions.reason: As in English (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: wana wa nuru, with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English offers "sons" as the traditional alternative to "children". Swahili "wana" (plural of "mwana", child) already means sons and daughters alike, so it serves both, and there is no span. Readable says "watu walio wa nuru" (people who belong to the light), as the English does.

decisions.choice: was hidden: he hid himself
decisions.reason: The verb is passive in form, as in 8:59, but it means that Jesus hid himself; no one else hid him. It is the same form used there when he left the temple.

decisions.choice: the end of Jesus's public teaching: the light withdraws
decisions.reason: This is Jesus's last public appeal in John. What he warned of in 12:35 begins to happen: the light is withdrawn from those who would not believe. The narrator now looks back on the response to his signs (12:37-43); from chapter 13 Jesus speaks to his disciples.

decisions.choice: hid himself (B); hid from the people (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the meaning of the passive form (meaning decision m1); Literal keeps "was hidden". Readable says "the people" for "them", the crowd of 12:34.

decisions.choice: se ocultó (L); se escondió (B, R)
decisions.reason: He hid himself (meaning decision m1); Spanish says it with the reflexive at every level.
